verdict.line: You lose if you throw Q or W into a charged Defiant Dance or engage below 50 Fury; you win if you force the fight the moment her E (Flawless Duet) is down and your Fury is stacked.

brief.thesis: This lane is a genuine coinflip, not a stat advantage for either side: Renekton's win condition is landing his 50-Fury threshold on W (Ruthless Predator) and E (Slice and Dice) inside her cooldown windows, while Irelia's is sustaining through Q (Bladesurge) heals and shrugging off damage during W (Defiant Dance) charges. Whoever tracks the other's cooldowns and resource bar more precisely wins the exchange, which is exactly why the numbers land at 50.9%.

theirWindow.what: She takes reduced physical damage while charging, so any Q or W you throw into it is wasted; step out of range or hold your combo, then punish immediately after since Defiant Dance's cooldown (20/18/16/14/12s) leaves her without it for a while.

yourWindow.what: W upgrades to a 3-hit, 1.5s stun that destroys shields instead of the base 0.75s stun, and Q's damage and heal both increase; bank Fury on autos before you commit, then chain empowered W into empowered E for a full stun-lock trade.

start.why: Run by 83.8% of Renektons in this matchup (51.2% WR over 1161 games) because the extra sustain and stats matter when your W requires standing at 300 range to land the stun.

boots.why: The dominant pick (89.5% pick rate, 51.9% WR over 1182 games); Irelia's damage comes from stacked Ionian Fervor autos, so flat physical reduction directly blunts her scaling.

core.why: First item in the most-played and highest win-rate path (60.5% over 172 games); the burst-damage proc rewards landing your stun combo.
Stacking armor shred compounds with your empowered E's own Armor reduction, letting your later autos and W hit harder through her defenses.
Completes the most-sampled core build; the damage-over-time conversion lets you win extended trades against her Q sustain instead of losing the burst race.

situational.when: you need more survivability against burst or all-in pressure (68.3% WR over 82 games in this alt path)
you're ahead and want to snowball cooldowns and damage faster (58.3% WR over 36 games in this alt path)
her Q (Bladesurge) healing and resets are keeping her alive through your trades
the enemy team stacks hard crowd control alongside her E (Flawless Duet) stun

runes.keystoneWhy: The most-played page (39.4% pick, 51.8% WR); Conqueror's stacking healing rewards the repeated Q/W/E trades this matchup forces, keeping you ahead in fights that run past the first stun since Irelia's own Q heal and W damage reduction extend skirmishes.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (89.9% pick rate, 51.9% WR); Ignite converts your Fury-stacked all-ins into kills in a matchup with no clean kill edge, and Flash covers the gap when your E (450 range) can't quite reach a retreating target.

playing.title: Bait her W before all-in
playing.detail: Defiant Dance reduces the physical damage she takes while charging, so don't throw Q or W into it; wait it out or disengage, then punish once it's down since its cooldown (20/18/16/14/12s) leaves her exposed.

playing.title: Track her E cooldown
playing.detail: Flawless Duet stuns and Marks on hit with a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown; once it's used, she loses her stun tool and her Q reset setup, making this your best window to commit.

playing.title: Hold W until 50+ Fury
playing.detail: Below 50 Fury, Ruthless Predator only stuns 0.75s over two hits; above 50 it becomes a 1.5s, three-hit stun that also destroys shields, letting you land a full follow-up combo instead of a half-trade.

playing.title: Don't feed Q resets
playing.detail: Bladesurge refreshes its cooldown if it hits a Marked target or kills, so if her E has just Marked you, disengage rather than trading through it and handing her a free reset.

playing.title: Empower E for the armor shred
playing.detail: Slice and Dice above 50 Fury deals bonus damage and lowers Armor on hit; bank Fury on autos first so the dash lands empowered and softens her for the stun that follows.

playing.title: Use Dominus to force all-ins
playing.detail: Dominus grants bonus Health and periodic Fury generation once it comes online at level 6, letting you commit to extended fights she can't out-sustain even with her Q heal.

playing.title: End fights fast past max stacks
playing.detail: At maximum Ionian Fervor stacks she gains bonus on-hit damage plus attack speed, so a fight that runs past 4-5 exchanged hits starts favoring her; close it out with your stun-lock burst rather than trading toe-to-toe.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch at this matchup's sample sizes; the cooldown-tracking and trade-window reasoning is my own read of the kit, not part of the stat line.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out on Irelia’s (P) stacks before engaging combat. Slowly build up Fury and avoid using your skills when Irelia uses (W).
